_comment: External dependency: the pi_agent_rust GitHub release this extension is built and tested against. `tag` is the SINGLE pinned value — bump only it to move the supported floor. The managed download (src/rust-install.ts) fetches this tag; the README 'Rust Pi (tested)' badge reads it; a user-supplied binary of a different version gets a one-time warning (src/extension.ts). Dependabot can't track GitHub releases natively — .github/workflows/upstream-currency.yml opens an issue when a newer release appears, using the `datasource`/`repo`/`tag` fields below.
_platformNote: LINUX GLIBC FLOOR. Upstream builds on a nightly toolchain and the floor moves between releases: v0.3.0 needs GLIBC_2.39, v0.5.1 needs 2.43 (measured with objdump -T on the linux arm64 and amd64 assets). 2.43 is newer than Debian 13 (2.41), Ubuntu 24.04 (2.39), Debian 12 (2.36) and Ubuntu 22.04 (2.35), so on those hosts the managed download cannot exec. That is now a HANDLED case rather than a hazard: the managed install probes the binary it just wrote, deletes it when it will not run, and names the glibc version the release needs (src/rust-install.ts); a configured-but-unrunnable rustBinaryPath is reported instead of silently substituted (src/rust-resolver.ts); and a readiness timeout carries the linker's own complaint (src/rust-process.ts). Linux users below the floor keep their existing binary and are told why. macOS and Windows are unaffected. Re-measure the floor when bumping this pin.
